answer:
**Chevrolet** released the most SUVs in 2014.  

The 2014 J.D. Power Vehicle Dependability Study lists three distinct Chevrolet SUV models that were awarded in the “SUV, MPV, Van, Pickup” segment:

| Chevrolet SUV models (2014 award winners) | # of models |
|-------------------------------------------|-------------|
| Chevrolet Equinox (Compact SUV) | 1 |
| Chevrolet Suburban (Compact‑Premium SUV) | 1 |
| Chevrolet Tahoe (Large SUV) | 1 |
| **Total Chevrolet SUVs** | **3** |

In comparison, the other brands mentioned in the same study offered fewer SUVs:

| Brand | SUV models in the study | # of models |
|-------|------------------------|-------------|
| GMC | GMC Terrain, GMC Yukon | 2 |
| Ford | Ford Edge (only Compact SUV in the study) | 1 |
| Toyota | Toyota Tacoma (Single Small SUV) | 1 |
| Others (e.g., Honda, Nissan, Pontiac, etc.) | 0–1 | 0–1 |

Thus, Chevrolet had the highest count of SUV models recognized by J.D. Power in 2014.

Title: Top-Ranked Cars, Trucks and SUVs in the J.D. Power 2014 APEAL Study
Chunks: 0,1,2,3,4
The annual _J.D. Power U.S. Automotive Performance, Execution, and Layout (APEAL) Study__SM_ measures how gratifying new vehicles are to own and drive after 90 days of ownership. In other words, it determines a vehicle's overall appeal. Based on the results of the _2014 APEAL Study_, the following models receive an award for ranking at the top of their respective vehicle segments. The award recipients are displayed in alphabetical order by make and model.
**2014 Audi A8**
This year, in the Large Premium Car segment, the Audi A8 ties with the completely redesigned Mercedes-Benz S-Class. For 2014, the A8 lineup expanded with the addition of the 3.0 TDI turbo-diesel model, and Audi installed additional standard features while making 22-way power ventilated front seats, ventilated rear seats, and massaging rear seats more widely available.
**2014 Audi Q5**
Leading the Compact Premium SUV segment, the Audi Q5 lineup expanded for 2014 to include a new TDI turbo-diesel model designed to get up to 31 mpg and a performance-oriented SQ5 variant equipped with a 354-horsepower, supercharged V-6 engine.
**2014 BMW 4 Series**
New for 2014 and offered in coupe and convertible body styles, the BMW 4 Series is based on the 3 Series and effectively replaces the previous 3 Series coupe and convertible models. Available as the 428i and 435i with rear-wheel or all-wheel drive, the 4 Series is the most appealing Compact Premium Car in this year's _APEAL Study_.
**2014 Dodge Challenger**
Among owners of Midsize Sporty Cars, those who buy the Dodge Challenger rate it the most appealing model, ahead of the Chevrolet Camaro and Ford Mustang. In 2014, Dodge offered new Hemi-powered Shaker models, additional limited-production variants, and new Scat Pack performance upgrades that don't void the factory warranty.
**2014 Dodge Charger**

In the Large Car segment, the Dodge Charger ranks highest, ahead of the Chevrolet SS and Kia Cadenza. Changes for 2014 included a new Charger Sport model with all-wheel drive, new Redline package, and expanded availability of big wheels and tires and a sport suspension to less-expensive versions.
**2014 Dodge Dart**
In the Compact Car segment of the _2014 APEAL Study_, the Dodge Dart is ranked highest. For 2014, Dodge replaced last year's turbocharged 4-cylinder engine and dual-clutch automated manual transmission on all Dart models, except the fuel-efficient Aero version, with a more conventional 4-cylinder and automatic transmission. Dodge also simplified the Dart lineup and the method buyers use to option the car.
**2014 Ford F-150**
In its final year before a redesign that includes an all-aluminum body, the Ford F-150 is the most appealing Large Light Duty Pickup in this year's _APEAL Study_. Aside from the debut of a turbocharged Tremor performance model, few changes were made to the 2014 F-150.
**2014 Ford F-Series Super Duty**
Among Large Heavy Duty Pickup trucks, the F-Series Super Duty lineup receives an award for overall vehicle appeal. For 2014, towing and payload capacity increased, thanks to a revamped braking system.
**2014 GMC Yukon**
The 2014 GMC Yukon is named the most appealing Large SUV, just before a redesigned 2015 model arrived in showrooms. Aside from adding more standard equipment to the base model, the only change was the addition of a new paint color.
**2014 Honda Ridgeline**
Honda is working on a redesigned Ridgeline, due for the 2016 model year. In the meantime, buyers of the old truck like it well enough that the Ridgeline ranks higher than the Nissan Frontier and Toyota Tacoma among Midsize Pickup models. For 2014, Honda added a new SE trim level at the top of the lineup.
**2014 Hyundai Accent**

The entry-level Accent is the most appealing Small Car in the _J.D. Power 2014 APEAL Study_, ranked higher than the Ford Fiesta and Chevrolet Sonic. For 2014, Hyundai added standard features, improved the car's voice-recognition Bluetooth system, and installed new upgrades for upper trim levels.
**2014 Kia Soul**
Redesigned for 2014, the Kia Soul is the highest-ranked Compact Multi-Purpose Vehicle in terms of appeal. Larger and more refined than it was before, the latest version of the Soul offers modern technology and practicality wrapped up in a unique package.
**2014 Land Rover Range Rover**
Among the most appealing models regardless of price, the Land Rover Range Rover is the highest-ranked model in the Large Premium SUV category in the _2014 APEAL Study_. This year, a new supercharged V-6 engine replaced last year's standard V-8 engine, LED headlights are standard, adaptive cruise control is less expensive, and Autobiography models gained equipment.
**2014 Mazda 6**
Redesigned this year, the Mazda 6 is the most appealing Midsize Car for 2014, ahead of the Kia Optima and Hyundai Sonata. Offered only with a 4-cylinder engine, the Mazda 6 can be optioned with several technologies commonly available only on more expensive vehicles.
**2014 Mercedes-Benz CLS-Class**
Among Midsize Premium Cars, the Mercedes-Benz CLS-Class ranks as the most appealing model, ahead of the Audi A7 and Audi A6. For 2014, Mercedes added 4Matic all-wheel drive as standard equipment for the performance-tuned CLS63 AMG, and debuted a higher-performance CLS63 AMG S-Model.
**2014 Mercedes-Benz S-Class**
Completely redesigned, the 2014 S-Class ties with the Audi A8 as the most appealing Large Premium Car in the latest _J.D. Power APEAL Study_. Four variants, including two high-performance AMG models, range in price from $94,000 to $222,000. Next-generation infotainment and autonomous safety technologies highlight the newest family of S-Class models.
**2014 Mini Countryman**

Ranking higher than the Buick Encore and Volkswagen Tiguan, the Mini Countryman is the most appealing Small SUV in the _2014 APEAL Study_. New John Cooper Works appearance packages debuted this past year, and Mini made minor equipment changes, including the addition of a standard 3-passenger rear bench seat, replacing the previous bucket seats.
**2014 Nissan Quest**
According to the _2014 APEAL Study_, Nissan Quest owners like their minivans, and this model ranks higher than the popular Honda Odyssey and Toyota Sienna for overall appeal in 2014. Aside from new colors, no changes were made this year.
**2014 Nissan Rogue**
Completely redesigned, the 2014 Nissan Rogue receives an award for ranking highest among Compact SUVs in the _2014 APEAL Study_, ahead of the Ford Escape and Jeep Cherokee. It is one of two models in its class to offer 7-passenger seating, and is available with numerous infotainment and safety technologies.
**2014 Porsche 911**
The multitude of Porsche 911 variants collectively ranks highest for vehicle appeal among Midsize Premium Sporty Cars. This year, Targa, Turbo, and GT3 versions joined the 911 lineup.
**2014 Porsche Boxster**
The Porsche Boxster ranks higher than the Porsche Cayman and Nissan 370Z among Compact Premium Sporty Cars in the _J.D. Power 2014 APEAL Study_. One year following a complete redesign, the Boxster received few changes.
**2014 Porsche Cayenne**
Among Premium Midsize SUVs, the Porsche Cayenne ranks higher than do the BMW X5 and redesigned Land Rover Range Rover Sport. For 2014, a new Platinum Edition debuted at the lower end of the range while a high-performance Turbo S variant arrived as a range-topping flagship model.
**2014 Toyota Highlander**
Redesigned for 2014, the Toyota Highlander is the highest-ranked Midsize SUV in the _2014 APEAL Study_, followed by the Jeep Grand Cherokee and Dodge Durango. The Highlander offers seating for up to 8 people, and a choice between a 4-cylinder, V-6, or gas-electric hybrid powertrains.

**2014 Volkswagen GTI**
Compact Sporty Car buyers rate their Volkswagen GTIs higher in terms of appeal than do people purchasing the Hyundai Veloster and Mini Cooper. In advance of a redesigned 2015 model, the 2014 GTI was offered only as a 5-door hatchback.

## [PDF page 1]
J.D. Power Reports:  
Automakers Struggle to Impress Owners with Increased Usefulness of In-Vehicle Technologies  
And Features on All-New and Redesigned Models
Dodge and Porsche Each Receive Three Segment-Level Awards;  
Audi, Ford, Mercedes-Benz and Nissan Each Receive Two
WESTLAKE VILLAGE, Calif.: 23 July 2014 — Although manufacturers are putting more and more  
technologies and functionality in their new and redesigned models, satisfaction with these features is  
not significantly higher among owners of those models than among owners of carryover models,  
according to the J.D. Power 2014 U.S. Automotive Performance, Execution and Layout (APEAL) StudySM  
released today.
The APEAL Study, now in its 19th year, serves as the industry benchmark for new-vehicle appeal. Owners  
evaluate their vehicle across 77 attributes, which combine into an overall APEAL score that is measured  
on a 1,000-point scale.
The study finds that APEAL scores for all-new and redesigned models continue to see a lift in APEAL  
scores compared with carryover models (805 vs. 791, respectively). However, while satisfaction in areas  
such as fuel economy and the feel and styling of the interior is higher among owners of all-new and  
redesigned models than among owners of carryover models, there is less differentiation in terms of the  
usefulness of the controls and functions for navigation, voice recognition and other technology  
applications.
“Manufacturers often look to new features and technologies to keep their vehicles fresh and attractive,  
but designing systems that consumers find intuitive and easy to use has been a challenge,” said Renee  
Stephens, vice president of U.S. automotive at J.D. Power. “Newly launched models surpass carryovers in  
impressing owners with the look and feel of the vehicle. But as we also see in our 2014 Initial Quality  
Study, owners are not as comfortable with the functionality of the features. To differentiate new models  
from the pack, automakers must continue to design systems that are not just attractive, but also intuitive  
and easy to use.”

## [PDF page 1]
The overall APEAL score in 2014 averages 794, which is a 1-point decrease from 2013. Fuel economy is  
the only category in which there has been improvement year over year (+6 points), which is due in part  
to an average decline of 3 percent in fuel prices during the survey period, compared with 2013. Owner-  
reported average mpg also improves to 25.0 mpg from 24.5 in 2013, resulting in more favorable  
perceptions of both driving range and mileage.
“Despite improvements this year, fuel economy continues to be the lowest-scoring category in the study  
by a wide margin,” said Stephens. “While many factors influence the fuel performance of a vehicle, an  
important factor is how the engine and transmission are tuned by the manufacturers. Automakers must  
find the right balance between owner expectations of fuel economy and areas that affect the driving  
experience, such as horsepower and transmission performance, which is not an easy task. Customers are  
not always happy with the trade-off between those characteristics.”
(Page 1 of 2)

## [PDF page 2]
2014 APEAL Rankings Highlights
Porsche is the highest-ranked nameplate in APEAL for the 10th consecutive year. Hyundai ranks highest  
among non-premium brands in the study. Hyundai is also the highest-ranked non-premium brand in the  
J.D. Power 2014 Initial Quality StudySM (IQS), marking the first time a nameplate has ranked highest  
among non-premium brands in both APEAL and IQS in the same year.
Both Dodge and Porsche receive three segment awards each: Dodge for the Challenger, Charger and  
Dart; and Porsche for the 911, Boxster and Cayenne.
Receiving two segment awards each are Audi, Ford, Mercedes-Benz and Nissan: Audi for the A8 (tie) and  
Q5; Ford for the F-150 LD and F-250/F-350 Super Duty; Mercedes-Benz for the CLS-Class and S-Class  
(tie); and Nissan for the Rogue and Quest.
Also receiving awards are the BMW 4 Series; GMC Yukon; Honda Ridgeline; Hyundai Accent; Kia Soul;  
Land Rover Range Rover; Mazda MAZDA6; MINI Countryman; Toyota Highlander; and Volkswagen GTI.
The APEAL Study examines how gratifying a new vehicle is to own and drive. The study is used  
extensively by manufacturers worldwide to help them design and develop more appealing vehicles and  
by consumers to help them in their purchase decisions. The 2014 APEAL Study is based on responses  
gathered between February and May 2014 from more than 86,000 purchasers and lessees of new 2014  
model-year cars and light trucks who were surveyed after the first 90 days of ownership. The APEAL  
Study complements the Initial Quality Study (IQS), which focuses on problems experienced by owners  
during the first 90 days of ownership.

The annual _J.D. Power U.S. Automotive Performance, Execution, and Layout (APEAL) Study__SM_ measures how gratifying new vehicles are to own and drive after 90 days of ownership. In other words, it determines a vehicle's overall appeal. Based on the results of the _2014 APEAL Study_, the following models receive an award for ranking at the top of their respective vehicle segments. The award recipients are displayed in alphabetical order by make and model.
**2014 Audi A8**
This year, in the Large Premium Car segment, the Audi A8 ties with the completely redesigned Mercedes-Benz S-Class. For 2014, the A8 lineup expanded with the addition of the 3.0 TDI turbo-diesel model, and Audi installed additional standard features while making 22-way power ventilated front seats, ventilated rear seats, and massaging rear seats more widely available.
**2014 Audi Q5**
Leading the Compact Premium SUV segment, the Audi Q5 lineup expanded for 2014 to include a new TDI turbo-diesel model designed to get up to 31 mpg and a performance-oriented SQ5 variant equipped with a 354-horsepower, supercharged V-6 engine.
**2014 BMW 4 Series**
New for 2014 and offered in coupe and convertible body styles, the BMW 4 Series is based on the 3 Series and effectively replaces the previous 3 Series coupe and convertible models. Available as the 428i and 435i with rear-wheel or all-wheel drive, the 4 Series is the most appealing Compact Premium Car in this year's _APEAL Study_.
**2014 Dodge Challenger**
Among owners of Midsize Sporty Cars, those who buy the Dodge Challenger rate it the most appealing model, ahead of the Chevrolet Camaro and Ford Mustang. In 2014, Dodge offered new Hemi-powered Shaker models, additional limited-production variants, and new Scat Pack performance upgrades that don't void the factory warranty.
**2014 Dodge Charger**
texts.1:
In the Large Car segment, the Dodge Charger ranks highest, ahead of the Chevrolet SS and Kia Cadenza. Changes for 2014 included a new Charger Sport model with all-wheel drive, new Redline package, and expanded availability of big wheels and tires and a sport suspension to less-expensive versions.
**2014 Dodge Dart**
In the Compact Car segment of the _2014 APEAL Study_, the Dodge Dart is ranked highest. For 2014, Dodge replaced last year's turbocharged 4-cylinder engine and dual-clutch automated manual transmission on all Dart models, except the fuel-efficient Aero version, with a more conventional 4-cylinder and automatic transmission. Dodge also simplified the Dart lineup and the method buyers use to option the car.
**2014 Ford F-150**
In its final year before a redesign that includes an all-aluminum body, the Ford F-150 is the most appealing Large Light Duty Pickup in this year's _APEAL Study_. Aside from the debut of a turbocharged Tremor performance model, few changes were made to the 2014 F-150.
**2014 Ford F-Series Super Duty**
Among Large Heavy Duty Pickup trucks, the F-Series Super Duty lineup receives an award for overall vehicle appeal. For 2014, towing and payload capacity increased, thanks to a revamped braking system.
**2014 GMC Yukon**
The 2014 GMC Yukon is named the most appealing Large SUV, just before a redesigned 2015 model arrived in showrooms. Aside from adding more standard equipment to the base model, the only change was the addition of a new paint color.
**2014 Honda Ridgeline**
Honda is working on a redesigned Ridgeline, due for the 2016 model year. In the meantime, buyers of the old truck like it well enough that the Ridgeline ranks higher than the Nissan Frontier and Toyota Tacoma among Midsize Pickup models. For 2014, Honda added a new SE trim level at the top of the lineup.
**2014 Hyundai Accent**
texts.2:
The entry-level Accent is the most appealing Small Car in the _J.D. Power 2014 APEAL Study_, ranked higher than the Ford Fiesta and Chevrolet Sonic. For 2014, Hyundai added standard features, improved the car's voice-recognition Bluetooth system, and installed new upgrades for upper trim levels.
**2014 Kia Soul**
Redesigned for 2014, the Kia Soul is the highest-ranked Compact Multi-Purpose Vehicle in terms of appeal. Larger and more refined than it was before, the latest version of the Soul offers modern technology and practicality wrapped up in a unique package.
**2014 Land Rover Range Rover**
Among the most appealing models regardless of price, the Land Rover Range Rover is the highest-ranked model in the Large Premium SUV category in the _2014 APEAL Study_. This year, a new supercharged V-6 engine replaced last year's standard V-8 engine, LED headlights are standard, adaptive cruise control is less expensive, and Autobiography models gained equipment.
**2014 Mazda 6**
Redesigned this year, the Mazda 6 is the most appealing Midsize Car for 2014, ahead of the Kia Optima and Hyundai Sonata. Offered only with a 4-cylinder engine, the Mazda 6 can be optioned with several technologies commonly available only on more expensive vehicles.
**2014 Mercedes-Benz CLS-Class**
Among Midsize Premium Cars, the Mercedes-Benz CLS-Class ranks as the most appealing model, ahead of the Audi A7 and Audi A6. For 2014, Mercedes added 4Matic all-wheel drive as standard equipment for the performance-tuned CLS63 AMG, and debuted a higher-performance CLS63 AMG S-Model.
**2014 Mercedes-Benz S-Class**
Completely redesigned, the 2014 S-Class ties with the Audi A8 as the most appealing Large Premium Car in the latest _J.D. Power APEAL Study_. Four variants, including two high-performance AMG models, range in price from $94,000 to $222,000. Next-generation infotainment and autonomous safety technologies highlight the newest family of S-Class models.
**2014 Mini Countryman**
texts.3:
Ranking higher than the Buick Encore and Volkswagen Tiguan, the Mini Countryman is the most appealing Small SUV in the _2014 APEAL Study_. New John Cooper Works appearance packages debuted this past year, and Mini made minor equipment changes, including the addition of a standard 3-passenger rear bench seat, replacing the previous bucket seats.
**2014 Nissan Quest**
According to the _2014 APEAL Study_, Nissan Quest owners like their minivans, and this model ranks higher than the popular Honda Odyssey and Toyota Sienna for overall appeal in 2014. Aside from new colors, no changes were made this year.
**2014 Nissan Rogue**
Completely redesigned, the 2014 Nissan Rogue receives an award for ranking highest among Compact SUVs in the _2014 APEAL Study_, ahead of the Ford Escape and Jeep Cherokee. It is one of two models in its class to offer 7-passenger seating, and is available with numerous infotainment and safety technologies.
**2014 Porsche 911**
The multitude of Porsche 911 variants collectively ranks highest for vehicle appeal among Midsize Premium Sporty Cars. This year, Targa, Turbo, and GT3 versions joined the 911 lineup.
**2014 Porsche Boxster**
The Porsche Boxster ranks higher than the Porsche Cayman and Nissan 370Z among Compact Premium Sporty Cars in the _J.D. Power 2014 APEAL Study_. One year following a complete redesign, the Boxster received few changes.
**2014 Porsche Cayenne**
Among Premium Midsize SUVs, the Porsche Cayenne ranks higher than do the BMW X5 and redesigned Land Rover Range Rover Sport. For 2014, a new Platinum Edition debuted at the lower end of the range while a high-performance Turbo S variant arrived as a range-topping flagship model.
**2014 Toyota Highlander**
Redesigned for 2014, the Toyota Highlander is the highest-ranked Midsize SUV in the _2014 APEAL Study_, followed by the Jeep Grand Cherokee and Dodge Durango. The Highlander offers seating for up to 8 people, and a choice between a 4-cylinder, V-6, or gas-electric hybrid powertrains.
texts.4:
**2014 Volkswagen GTI**
Compact Sporty Car buyers rate their Volkswagen GTIs higher in terms of appeal than do people purchasing the Hyundai Veloster and Mini Cooper. In advance of a redesigned 2015 model, the 2014 GTI was offered only as a 5-door hatchback.

## [PDF page 1]
J.D. Power Reports:  
Automakers Struggle to Impress Owners with Increased Usefulness of In-Vehicle Technologies  
And Features on All-New and Redesigned Models
Dodge and Porsche Each Receive Three Segment-Level Awards;  
Audi, Ford, Mercedes-Benz and Nissan Each Receive Two
WESTLAKE VILLAGE, Calif.: 23 July 2014 — Although manufacturers are putting more and more  
technologies and functionality in their new and redesigned models, satisfaction with these features is  
not significantly higher among owners of those models than among owners of carryover models,  
according to the J.D. Power 2014 U.S. Automotive Performance, Execution and Layout (APEAL) StudySM  
released today.
The APEAL Study, now in its 19th year, serves as the industry benchmark for new-vehicle appeal. Owners  
evaluate their vehicle across 77 attributes, which combine into an overall APEAL score that is measured  
on a 1,000-point scale.
The study finds that APEAL scores for all-new and redesigned models continue to see a lift in APEAL  
scores compared with carryover models (805 vs. 791, respectively). However, while satisfaction in areas  
such as fuel economy and the feel and styling of the interior is higher among owners of all-new and  
redesigned models than among owners of carryover models, there is less differentiation in terms of the  
usefulness of the controls and functions for navigation, voice recognition and other technology  
applications.
“Manufacturers often look to new features and technologies to keep their vehicles fresh and attractive,  
but designing systems that consumers find intuitive and easy to use has been a challenge,” said Renee  
Stephens, vice president of U.S. automotive at J.D. Power. “Newly launched models surpass carryovers in  
impressing owners with the look and feel of the vehicle. But as we also see in our 2014 Initial Quality  
Study, owners are not as comfortable with the functionality of the features. To differentiate new models  
from the pack, automakers must continue to design systems that are not just attractive, but also intuitive  
and easy to use.”
texts.2:
## [PDF page 1]
The overall APEAL score in 2014 averages 794, which is a 1-point decrease from 2013. Fuel economy is  
the only category in which there has been improvement year over year (+6 points), which is due in part  
to an average decline of 3 percent in fuel prices during the survey period, compared with 2013. Owner-  
reported average mpg also improves to 25.0 mpg from 24.5 in 2013, resulting in more favorable  
perceptions of both driving range and mileage.
“Despite improvements this year, fuel economy continues to be the lowest-scoring category in the study  
by a wide margin,” said Stephens. “While many factors influence the fuel performance of a vehicle, an  
important factor is how the engine and transmission are tuned by the manufacturers. Automakers must  
find the right balance between owner expectations of fuel economy and areas that affect the driving  
experience, such as horsepower and transmission performance, which is not an easy task. Customers are  
not always happy with the trade-off between those characteristics.”
(Page 1 of 2)

## [PDF page 2]
2014 APEAL Rankings Highlights
Porsche is the highest-ranked nameplate in APEAL for the 10th consecutive year. Hyundai ranks highest  
among non-premium brands in the study. Hyundai is also the highest-ranked non-premium brand in the  
J.D. Power 2014 Initial Quality StudySM (IQS), marking the first time a nameplate has ranked highest  
among non-premium brands in both APEAL and IQS in the same year.
Both Dodge and Porsche receive three segment awards each: Dodge for the Challenger, Charger and  
Dart; and Porsche for the 911, Boxster and Cayenne.
Receiving two segment awards each are Audi, Ford, Mercedes-Benz and Nissan: Audi for the A8 (tie) and  
Q5; Ford for the F-150 LD and F-250/F-350 Super Duty; Mercedes-Benz for the CLS-Class and S-Class  
(tie); and Nissan for the Rogue and Quest.
Also receiving awards are the BMW 4 Series; GMC Yukon; Honda Ridgeline; Hyundai Accent; Kia Soul;  
Land Rover Range Rover; Mazda MAZDA6; MINI Countryman; Toyota Highlander; and Volkswagen GTI.
The APEAL Study examines how gratifying a new vehicle is to own and drive. The study is used  
extensively by manufacturers worldwide to help them design and develop more appealing vehicles and  
by consumers to help them in their purchase decisions. The 2014 APEAL Study is based on responses  
gathered between February and May 2014 from more than 86,000 purchasers and lessees of new 2014  
model-year cars and light trucks who were surveyed after the first 90 days of ownership. The APEAL  
Study complements the Initial Quality Study (IQS), which focuses on problems experienced by owners  
during the first 90 days of ownership.

The annual _J.D. Power U.S. Automotive Performance, Execution, and Layout (APEAL) Study__SM_ measures how gratifying new vehicles are to own and drive after 90 days of ownership. In other words, it determines a vehicle's overall appeal. Based on the results of the _2014 APEAL Study_, the following models receive an award for ranking at the top of their respective vehicle segments. The award recipients are displayed in alphabetical order by make and model.
**2014 Audi A8**
This year, in the Large Premium Car segment, the Audi A8 ties with the completely redesigned Mercedes-Benz S-Class. For 2014, the A8 lineup expanded with the addition of the 3.0 TDI turbo-diesel model, and Audi installed additional standard features while making 22-way power ventilated front seats, ventilated rear seats, and massaging rear seats more widely available.
**2014 Audi Q5**
Leading the Compact Premium SUV segment, the Audi Q5 lineup expanded for 2014 to include a new TDI turbo-diesel model designed to get up to 31 mpg and a performance-oriented SQ5 variant equipped with a 354-horsepower, supercharged V-6 engine.
**2014 BMW 4 Series**
New for 2014 and offered in coupe and convertible body styles, the BMW 4 Series is based on the 3 Series and effectively replaces the previous 3 Series coupe and convertible models. Available as the 428i and 435i with rear-wheel or all-wheel drive, the 4 Series is the most appealing Compact Premium Car in this year's _APEAL Study_.
**2014 Dodge Challenger**
Among owners of Midsize Sporty Cars, those who buy the Dodge Challenger rate it the most appealing model, ahead of the Chevrolet Camaro and Ford Mustang. In 2014, Dodge offered new Hemi-powered Shaker models, additional limited-production variants, and new Scat Pack performance upgrades that don't void the factory warranty.
**2014 Dodge Charger**

In the Large Car segment, the Dodge Charger ranks highest, ahead of the Chevrolet SS and Kia Cadenza. Changes for 2014 included a new Charger Sport model with all-wheel drive, new Redline package, and expanded availability of big wheels and tires and a sport suspension to less-expensive versions.
**2014 Dodge Dart**
In the Compact Car segment of the _2014 APEAL Study_, the Dodge Dart is ranked highest. For 2014, Dodge replaced last year's turbocharged 4-cylinder engine and dual-clutch automated manual transmission on all Dart models, except the fuel-efficient Aero version, with a more conventional 4-cylinder and automatic transmission. Dodge also simplified the Dart lineup and the method buyers use to option the car.
**2014 Ford F-150**
In its final year before a redesign that includes an all-aluminum body, the Ford F-150 is the most appealing Large Light Duty Pickup in this year's _APEAL Study_. Aside from the debut of a turbocharged Tremor performance model, few changes were made to the 2014 F-150.
**2014 Ford F-Series Super Duty**
Among Large Heavy Duty Pickup trucks, the F-Series Super Duty lineup receives an award for overall vehicle appeal. For 2014, towing and payload capacity increased, thanks to a revamped braking system.
**2014 GMC Yukon**
The 2014 GMC Yukon is named the most appealing Large SUV, just before a redesigned 2015 model arrived in showrooms. Aside from adding more standard equipment to the base model, the only change was the addition of a new paint color.
**2014 Honda Ridgeline**
Honda is working on a redesigned Ridgeline, due for the 2016 model year. In the meantime, buyers of the old truck like it well enough that the Ridgeline ranks higher than the Nissan Frontier and Toyota Tacoma among Midsize Pickup models. For 2014, Honda added a new SE trim level at the top of the lineup.
**2014 Hyundai Accent**

The entry-level Accent is the most appealing Small Car in the _J.D. Power 2014 APEAL Study_, ranked higher than the Ford Fiesta and Chevrolet Sonic. For 2014, Hyundai added standard features, improved the car's voice-recognition Bluetooth system, and installed new upgrades for upper trim levels.
**2014 Kia Soul**
Redesigned for 2014, the Kia Soul is the highest-ranked Compact Multi-Purpose Vehicle in terms of appeal. Larger and more refined than it was before, the latest version of the Soul offers modern technology and practicality wrapped up in a unique package.
**2014 Land Rover Range Rover**
Among the most appealing models regardless of price, the Land Rover Range Rover is the highest-ranked model in the Large Premium SUV category in the _2014 APEAL Study_. This year, a new supercharged V-6 engine replaced last year's standard V-8 engine, LED headlights are standard, adaptive cruise control is less expensive, and Autobiography models gained equipment.
**2014 Mazda 6**
Redesigned this year, the Mazda 6 is the most appealing Midsize Car for 2014, ahead of the Kia Optima and Hyundai Sonata. Offered only with a 4-cylinder engine, the Mazda 6 can be optioned with several technologies commonly available only on more expensive vehicles.
**2014 Mercedes-Benz CLS-Class**
Among Midsize Premium Cars, the Mercedes-Benz CLS-Class ranks as the most appealing model, ahead of the Audi A7 and Audi A6. For 2014, Mercedes added 4Matic all-wheel drive as standard equipment for the performance-tuned CLS63 AMG, and debuted a higher-performance CLS63 AMG S-Model.
**2014 Mercedes-Benz S-Class**
Completely redesigned, the 2014 S-Class ties with the Audi A8 as the most appealing Large Premium Car in the latest _J.D. Power APEAL Study_. Four variants, including two high-performance AMG models, range in price from $94,000 to $222,000. Next-generation infotainment and autonomous safety technologies highlight the newest family of S-Class models.
**2014 Mini Countryman**

Ranking higher than the Buick Encore and Volkswagen Tiguan, the Mini Countryman is the most appealing Small SUV in the _2014 APEAL Study_. New John Cooper Works appearance packages debuted this past year, and Mini made minor equipment changes, including the addition of a standard 3-passenger rear bench seat, replacing the previous bucket seats.
**2014 Nissan Quest**
According to the _2014 APEAL Study_, Nissan Quest owners like their minivans, and this model ranks higher than the popular Honda Odyssey and Toyota Sienna for overall appeal in 2014. Aside from new colors, no changes were made this year.
**2014 Nissan Rogue**
Completely redesigned, the 2014 Nissan Rogue receives an award for ranking highest among Compact SUVs in the _2014 APEAL Study_, ahead of the Ford Escape and Jeep Cherokee. It is one of two models in its class to offer 7-passenger seating, and is available with numerous infotainment and safety technologies.
**2014 Porsche 911**
The multitude of Porsche 911 variants collectively ranks highest for vehicle appeal among Midsize Premium Sporty Cars. This year, Targa, Turbo, and GT3 versions joined the 911 lineup.
**2014 Porsche Boxster**
The Porsche Boxster ranks higher than the Porsche Cayman and Nissan 370Z among Compact Premium Sporty Cars in the _J.D. Power 2014 APEAL Study_. One year following a complete redesign, the Boxster received few changes.
**2014 Porsche Cayenne**
Among Premium Midsize SUVs, the Porsche Cayenne ranks higher than do the BMW X5 and redesigned Land Rover Range Rover Sport. For 2014, a new Platinum Edition debuted at the lower end of the range while a high-performance Turbo S variant arrived as a range-topping flagship model.
**2014 Toyota Highlander**
Redesigned for 2014, the Toyota Highlander is the highest-ranked Midsize SUV in the _2014 APEAL Study_, followed by the Jeep Grand Cherokee and Dodge Durango. The Highlander offers seating for up to 8 people, and a choice between a 4-cylinder, V-6, or gas-electric hybrid powertrains.

**2014 Volkswagen GTI**
Compact Sporty Car buyers rate their Volkswagen GTIs higher in terms of appeal than do people purchasing the Hyundai Veloster and Mini Cooper. In advance of a redesigned 2015 model, the 2014 GTI was offered only as a 5-door hatchback.

J.D. Power Reports:  
Automakers Struggle to Impress Owners with Increased Usefulness of In-Vehicle Technologies  
And Features on All-New and Redesigned Models
Dodge and Porsche Each Receive Three Segment-Level Awards;  
Audi, Ford, Mercedes-Benz and Nissan Each Receive Two
WESTLAKE VILLAGE, Calif.: 23 July 2014 — Although manufacturers are putting more and more  
technologies and functionality in their new and redesigned models, satisfaction with these features is  
not significantly higher among owners of those models than among owners of carryover models,  
according to the J.D. Power 2014 U.S. Automotive Performance, Execution and Layout (APEAL) StudySM  
released today.
The APEAL Study, now in its 19th year, serves as the industry benchmark for new-vehicle appeal. Owners  
evaluate their vehicle across 77 attributes, which combine into an overall APEAL score that is measured  
on a 1,000-point scale.
The study finds that APEAL scores for all-new and redesigned models continue to see a lift in APEAL  
scores compared with carryover models (805 vs. 791, respectively). However, while satisfaction in areas  
such as fuel economy and the feel and styling of the interior is higher among owners of all-new and  
redesigned models than among owners of carryover models, there is less differentiation in terms of the  
usefulness of the controls and functions for navigation, voice recognition and other technology  
applications.
“Manufacturers often look to new features and technologies to keep their vehicles fresh and attractive,  
but designing systems that consumers find intuitive and easy to use has been a challenge,” said Renee  
Stephens, vice president of U.S. automotive at J.D. Power. “Newly launched models surpass carryovers in  
impressing owners with the look and feel of the vehicle. But as we also see in our 2014 Initial Quality  
Study, owners are not as comfortable with the functionality of the features. To differentiate new models  
from the pack, automakers must continue to design systems that are not just attractive, but also intuitive  
and easy to use.”

## [PDF page 1]
The overall APEAL score in 2014 averages 794, which is a 1-point decrease from 2013. Fuel economy is  
the only category in which there has been improvement year over year (+6 points), which is due in part  
to an average decline of 3 percent in fuel prices during the survey period, compared with 2013. Owner-  
reported average mpg also improves to 25.0 mpg from 24.5 in 2013, resulting in more favorable  
perceptions of both driving range and mileage.
“Despite improvements this year, fuel economy continues to be the lowest-scoring category in the study  
by a wide margin,” said Stephens. “While many factors influence the fuel performance of a vehicle, an  
important factor is how the engine and transmission are tuned by the manufacturers. Automakers must  
find the right balance between owner expectations of fuel economy and areas that affect the driving  
experience, such as horsepower and transmission performance, which is not an easy task. Customers are  
not always happy with the trade-off between those characteristics.”
(Page 1 of 2)

2014 APEAL Rankings Highlights
Porsche is the highest-ranked nameplate in APEAL for the 10th consecutive year. Hyundai ranks highest  
among non-premium brands in the study. Hyundai is also the highest-ranked non-premium brand in the  
J.D. Power 2014 Initial Quality StudySM (IQS), marking the first time a nameplate has ranked highest  
among non-premium brands in both APEAL and IQS in the same year.
Both Dodge and Porsche receive three segment awards each: Dodge for the Challenger, Charger and

The APEAL Study examines how gratifying a new vehicle is to own and drive. The study is used

## Common Questions About Buying Used SUVs
### Which SUV brands are most reliable for used buyers?
Toyota and Honda lead SUV reliability with extensive track records of durability and low ownership costs. The Toyota RAV4 averages just $386 annually in repairs versus $489 segment average, while the Honda CR-V earned Consumer Reports' top ratings and J.D. Power awards. Mazda SUVs like the CX-5 show exceptional reliability with only 0.6 unscheduled repair visits yearly versus 1.1 segment average. Subaru provides standard AWD across all models with above-average reliability, though AWD maintenance adds $200-500 annually. Kia and Hyundai dramatically improved reliability in recent years, with the Telluride and Palisade offering 10-year/100,000-mile powertrain warranties. Chevrolet's Traverse earned an 88/100 J.D. Power reliability rating, leading mid-size three-row SUVs. Lexus (Toyota's luxury division) delivers premium reliability, with the RX scoring 85/100 and the GX known for lasting 200,000+ miles. Domestic brands like Ford and Chevrolet offer good value with reasonable reliability, though maintenance costs run slightly higher than Japanese brands. Avoid European luxury SUVs from Mercedes-Benz and BMW in the used market due to significantly higher repair costs.

## Common Questions About Buying Used SUVs
### What should I inspect when test driving a used SUV?
Begin by checking all features before driving: test air conditioning, heating, radio, power windows, locks, and windshield wipers. Verify the backup camera displays clearly and that all interior lights function. Check that the liftgate opens and closes smoothly. Start the engine and listen for smooth, quiet operation without knocking, ticking, or unusual noises. During the test drive, accelerate firmly to ensure the engine responds without hesitation and the transmission shifts smoothly through all gears. Drive on highways to check for vibrations at 60-70 MPH and verify the cruise control works properly. Test brakes multiple times, ensuring the pedal feels firm and the SUV stops straight without pulling to either side. Make several turns to check steering responsiveness. If the SUV has AWD, verify the system engages properly (some vehicles have indicators or test modes). Check for adequate power when accelerating from a stop, especially important in three-row SUVs carrying passengers. Pay attention to visibility from the driver's seat, blind spots, and whether mirrors provide clear views. Listen for wind noise at highway speeds and rattles over bumps. After the test drive, check under the SUV for any fluid leaks.

## Common Questions About Buying Used SUVs
### Are SUVs really safer than sedans?
SUVs provide several safety advantages that combine structural benefits with modern technology. The elevated seating position improves visibility, allowing drivers to see traffic patterns, hazards, and brake lights farther ahead than sedan drivers sitting 6-12 inches lower. Greater size and weight reduce collision forces on occupants during impacts. Modern SUVs include comprehensive safety technology as standard equipment: automatic emergency braking with pedestrian detection, blind-spot monitoring with rear cross-traffic alert, and lane keeping assist have become baseline features on most 2018-2020 models. Statistics support this perception, with 58% of SUV buyers reporting feeling safer in larger vehicles. Insurance costs reflect actual safety performance, with SUVs averaging $1,935 annually versus $2,120 for sedans, a $185 annual savings indicating lower injury claim rates. However, proper safety depends on vehicle condition and driver behavior more than vehicle type. Any well-maintained SUV or sedan with modern safety features provides excellent protection. The IIHS and NHTSA test both vehicle types rigorously, and top-rated sedans and SUVs perform comparably in crashes. The practical advantage of SUVs comes from better visibility and handling difficult weather or road conditions confidently.

## Common Questions About Buying Used SUVs
### What maintenance costs should I expect with an SUV?
Mainstream SUVs cost $792-900 annually to maintain according to AAA data, comparable to sedan maintenance. This includes regular oil changes every 5,000-7,500 miles ($40-70 each), tire rotations, brake service, and routine inspections. Toyota and Honda lead with lowest costs: the RAV4 averages just $386 annually while the CR-V shows below-average repair frequency. The Mazda CX-5 requires only 0.6 unscheduled repair visits yearly. AWD systems add $200-500 annually compared to FWD vehicles due to additional components requiring service. Larger SUVs face higher tire replacement costs, with sets running $800-$1,500 compared to $600-$1,000 for compact SUVs. European luxury SUVs carry significantly higher costs: Mercedes-Benz maintenance runs double Lincoln's costs over 10 years, while Porsche averages $1,623 annually. Proper maintenance dramatically affects longevity. Follow the manufacturer's service schedule precisely, address minor issues promptly before they become expensive problems, and use quality parts. Well-maintained Toyotas and Hondas routinely exceed 200,000 miles with reasonable repair costs. Keep service records organized and address any unusual noises, vibrations, or warning lights immediately.

## Common Questions About Buying Used SUVs
### Do I need special features for upstate South Carolina weather?
Upstate South Carolina's humid subtropical climate requires specific considerations but not extreme weather equipment. The region receives 47-50 inches of annual rainfall, making AWD beneficial for confident driving in heavy rain and on wet roads, though quality FWD with good all-season tires proves adequate for most situations. AWD shows its value during occasional winter ice events and when accessing unpaved roads to outdoor recreation areas. Ground clearance of 8+ inches handles unpaved access roads to state park trailheads and boat launches without difficulty. Standard modern features address the climate well: working air conditioning proves essential during humid summers (test it thoroughly during purchase), rear climate vents keep passengers comfortable, and heated seats extend comfortable outdoor season into cooler months. The region's mild winters (rarely significant snow at 800-1,000 foot elevations) don't require the winter packages or extreme cold weather features needed in northern climates. Instead, prioritize features for the active outdoor lifestyle: roof rails for kayaks and bikes to area lakes and trails, easy-clean interior materials that tolerate dirt and water from outdoor activities, and adequate cargo space for camping gear. Quality all-season tires matter more than AWD for most drivers, though many buyers choose AWD for the 5-7% fuel economy penalty given the region's outdoor recreation emphasis.

## Common Questions About Buying Used SUVs
### Should I buy a hybrid SUV or stick with traditional gas engines?
Hybrid SUVs dramatically narrow the fuel economy gap with sedans while maintaining full SUV capability. The Toyota RAV4 Hybrid achieves 40 MPG combined versus 30 MPG for the gas model, saving approximately $600-800 annually for a driver covering 15,000 miles at $3.50/gallon. The Honda CR-V Hybrid reaches 38 MPG combined. These hybrids cost $3,000-5,000 more used than gas equivalents, but fuel savings recover this premium in 4-6 years while providing the same cargo space, seating, and towing capability. Hybrid systems prove particularly efficient in stop-and-go traffic and city driving, ideal for Spartanburg and Greenville commuters. Reliability concerns have largely disappeared with modern hybrids: Toyota's hybrid system has proven durable over 20+ years and millions of vehicles. Battery warranties typically cover 8-10 years or 100,000 miles. Maintenance costs run slightly higher due to additional components, but this difference is minor compared to fuel savings. The practical consideration is purchase price: if your budget allows the $3,000-5,000 hybrid premium on a used SUV, the fuel savings and reduced environmental impact make it worthwhile. If budget is tighter, a well-maintained gas SUV provides excellent service with slightly higher fuel costs but lower initial investment.

Source: https://www.jdpower.com/cars/2022/jeep/grand-cherokee-4xe
Title: 2022 Jeep Grand Cherokee Reliability, Consumer Ratings & Pricing
Chunks: 0,1,2,3,4,5
### **Introduction - Find the best Jeep deals!**
Jeepis a globally aspirational brand, defined mainly by the iconicWranglerand its ancestors. Top and doors off, the Wrangler epitomizes the rugged individualism and spirit of adventure that characterizes America and its citizens. It is a rolling symbol of fun, freedom, and determination. But,as people who buy the Wrangler often find out, idealizing ownership of one and actually driving one every day are two completely different things.
That's where theJeep Grand Cherokeecomes in. Like the Wrangler, the Grand Cherokee seats up to five people and can go places and do things that mostSUVscan't. Unlike the Wrangler, the Grand Cherokee is a civilized daily driver, comfortable, quiet, and far more refined. You can't remove the roof and doors, but you'll also be a much happier camper most of the time.
Redesigned for 2022, the Grand Cherokee comes in two flavors. The first is the 2-row, 5-passenger version that is the subject of this review. The second is the 3-row, 7-passenger version that debuted in 2021. You canlearn more about the 2021 Jeep Grand Cherokee L by reading this full review of the SUV.
The 5-passenger 2022 Grand Cherokee lineup launches with Laredo, Altitude, Limited, Trailhawk, Overland, Summit, and Summit Reserve trim levels. Initially, Jeep offers a standard V6 engine with rear-wheel (RWD) or 4-wheel drive (4WD), or a V8 engine with 4WD. A Grand Cherokee 4xeplug-in hybrid electric(PHEV) model arrives in 2022.
In addition to the first electrified version of the nameplate, highlights of the redesigned 2022 Jeep Grand Cherokee include significant infotainment, convenience, and safety technology improvements combined with the traditional styling, driving dynamics, and off-roading capabilities that have characterized the model for decades.

### **What Owners Say About the Jeep Grand Cherokee - Find the best Jeep deals!**
****
_**Photo: Christian Wardlaw**_
The Jeep Grand Cherokee competes in the Midsize SUV market segment. According to data collected from verified new-vehicle buyers for the_JD Power 2021 Automotive Performance, Execution and Layout (APEAL) Study_, 56% of previous-generation Jeep Grand Cherokee buyers are male, exactly matching the Midsize SUV segment. The median age of a Grand Cherokee buyer is 57 years (vs. 58 for the segment).
As part of the _APEAL Study_, owners rated the Grand Cherokee in 10 primary categories. Listed below in descending order, you'll find their preferences from their most favorite thing about the vehicle to their least favorite:
*   Exterior styling  
*   Driving feel  
*   Feeling of safety  
*   Interior design (in a tie with powertrain)  
*   Powertrain (in a tie with interior design)  
*   Driving comfort (in a tie with setting up and starting)  
*   Setting up and starting (in a tie with driving comfort)  
*   Getting in and out  
*   Infotainment system  
*   Fuel economy
In the _2021 APEAL Study_, the previous-generation Grand Cherokee ranks fifth out of eight Midsize SUV models.

### **What Our Independent Expert Says About the Jeep Grand Cherokee - Find the best Jeep deals!**
In the sections that follow, our independent expert provides an analysis of the new Grand Cherokee based on experience driving the following versions of the SUV in the Moab, Utah area:
*   Laredo with a V6 and optional Quadra-Trac I 4WD  
*   Limited with a V6 and optional Quadra-Trac I 4WD  
*   Trailhawk with a V6 and optional Quadra-Drive II 4WD  
*   Overland with a V8 and the required Quadra-Trac II 4WD  
*   Summit Reserve with a V6 and standard Quadra-Drive II 4WD
Prices of the test vehicles ranged from $44,765 to $70,695, including the $1,795 destination charge.

### _Getting In and Getting Comfortable_
****
_**Photo: Christian Wardlaw**_
Unless you've raised the available Quadra-Lift airsuspensionto maximize ground clearance, as I did during an off-roading adventure in the Grand Cherokee Trailhawk, this SUV is easy enough to get into and out of. That's especially true if you kneel the SUV's air suspension using the Exit Mode, which drops the Grand Cherokee to its lowest setting in just seven seconds.
Regardless of the trim level, each test vehicle had a power-adjustable driver's seat that offered plenty of comfort and support. Even the cloth-upholstered Laredo had heated front seats and a heated steering wheel, and the Summit Reserve's supple premium leather chairs came with ventilation and a massage function.
Once you're aboard, you'll discover improved outward visibility compared to the previous-generation Grand Cherokee. Partly, this is due to the lower beltline and greater glass area. Still, the new Grand Cherokee also offers a variety of camera views, including a rear camera mirror and an off-roading camera that looks forward and, on the display screen, overlays the projected tire path onto the upcoming terrain.
The control layout is straightforward, but the gloss black trim in some models can suffer from reflections that make them hard to see and use. Also, Jeep uses a rotary knob for a shifter, and it took me a few tries to get the hang of it. Too often, I chose Drive instead of Park, released the brake, and started to get out before realizing the dang thing was moving.
A 10.25-inch digital instrumentation display is standard, and most versions include an 8.4-inch touchscreen infotainment system. A larger 10.1-inch screen is available in all but Laredo trim. Beneath the infotainment system, a mix of stereo and climate controls offers quick access to frequently used functions.

### _Getting In and Getting Comfortable_
Every version of the Grand Cherokee reflects quality. In fact, when you drive the Laredo, it feels more substantial than you expect of a base-trim model. Many vehicles feel engineered to a minimum standard and then get extra sound-deadening material, leather, wood, and technology in order to pass the premium test. By contrast, the new Grand Cherokee sounds and feels like it is built to a higher standard, and then Jeep figured out how to discount it to hit the Laredo's price point. In any case, if your budget dictates getting the Laredo, you won't feel like you settled for less.
Rear-seat room is tight for adults, and the hard plastic front seatbacks are painful when knees and shins encounter them. Grand Cherokee buyers who plan to transport taller passengers regularly will want the roomier Grand Cherokee L model.

### _2022 Jeep Grand Cherokee Uconnect 5 Infotainment System Review_
****
_**Photo: Christian Wardlaw**_
According to Jeep, the Grand Cherokee's newUconnect 5infotainment technology offers a dramatically faster response to inputs, crisp and clean high-resolution graphics, greater ability to customize content and save preferences, and an improved user experience.Over-the-air software updatesimprove the technology over time.
Highlights of the Grand Cherokee's standard Uconnect 5 system include:
*   8.4-inch touchscreen display  
*   Bluetooth connectivity for two smartphones  
*   Wireless Apple CarPlay and Android Auto  
*   Amazon Alexa integration  
*   SiriusXM 360L satellite radio
Depending on the trim level and equipment, upgrades include:
*   Navigation  
*   SiriusXM Guardianconnected services  
*   9-speaker Alpine premium sound system  
*   19-speaker McIntosh high-end audio system
Pairing my iPhone XS to Bluetooth was not a problem, and setting up personal preferences is relatively easy—especially if you're comfortable with modern technology. The voice-recognition system also works well, responding quickly and accurately to nearly all my standard test commands and questions.
There is a clear progression in terms of audio system quality. The basic setup in the Laredo was merely adequate, and the Alpine speakers in the Limited were an improvement. But they didn't come anywhere close to the outstanding McIntosh components in the Overland and Summit Reserve test vehicles.

## Common Questions About Buying Used SUVs
### Which SUV brands are most reliable for used buyers?
Toyota and Honda lead SUV reliability with extensive track records of durability and low ownership costs. The Toyota RAV4 averages just $386 annually in repairs versus $489 segment average, while the Honda CR-V earned Consumer Reports' top ratings and J.D. Power awards. Mazda SUVs like the CX-5 show exceptional reliability with only 0.6 unscheduled repair visits yearly versus 1.1 segment average. Subaru provides standard AWD across all models with above-average reliability, though AWD maintenance adds $200-500 annually. Kia and Hyundai dramatically improved reliability in recent years, with the Telluride and Palisade offering 10-year/100,000-mile powertrain warranties. Chevrolet's Traverse earned an 88/100 J.D. Power reliability rating, leading mid-size three-row SUVs. Lexus (Toyota's luxury division) delivers premium reliability, with the RX scoring 85/100 and the GX known for lasting 200,000+ miles. Domestic brands like Ford and Chevrolet offer good value with reasonable reliability, though maintenance costs run slightly higher than Japanese brands. Avoid European luxury SUVs from Mercedes-Benz and BMW in the used market due to significantly higher repair costs.
texts.31:
## Common Questions About Buying Used SUVs
### What should I inspect when test driving a used SUV?
Begin by checking all features before driving: test air conditioning, heating, radio, power windows, locks, and windshield wipers. Verify the backup camera displays clearly and that all interior lights function. Check that the liftgate opens and closes smoothly. Start the engine and listen for smooth, quiet operation without knocking, ticking, or unusual noises. During the test drive, accelerate firmly to ensure the engine responds without hesitation and the transmission shifts smoothly through all gears. Drive on highways to check for vibrations at 60-70 MPH and verify the cruise control works properly. Test brakes multiple times, ensuring the pedal feels firm and the SUV stops straight without pulling to either side. Make several turns to check steering responsiveness. If the SUV has AWD, verify the system engages properly (some vehicles have indicators or test modes). Check for adequate power when accelerating from a stop, especially important in three-row SUVs carrying passengers. Pay attention to visibility from the driver's seat, blind spots, and whether mirrors provide clear views. Listen for wind noise at highway speeds and rattles over bumps. After the test drive, check under the SUV for any fluid leaks.
texts.32:
## Common Questions About Buying Used SUVs
### Are SUVs really safer than sedans?
SUVs provide several safety advantages that combine structural benefits with modern technology. The elevated seating position improves visibility, allowing drivers to see traffic patterns, hazards, and brake lights farther ahead than sedan drivers sitting 6-12 inches lower. Greater size and weight reduce collision forces on occupants during impacts. Modern SUVs include comprehensive safety technology as standard equipment: automatic emergency braking with pedestrian detection, blind-spot monitoring with rear cross-traffic alert, and lane keeping assist have become baseline features on most 2018-2020 models. Statistics support this perception, with 58% of SUV buyers reporting feeling safer in larger vehicles. Insurance costs reflect actual safety performance, with SUVs averaging $1,935 annually versus $2,120 for sedans, a $185 annual savings indicating lower injury claim rates. However, proper safety depends on vehicle condition and driver behavior more than vehicle type. Any well-maintained SUV or sedan with modern safety features provides excellent protection. The IIHS and NHTSA test both vehicle types rigorously, and top-rated sedans and SUVs perform comparably in crashes. The practical advantage of SUVs comes from better visibility and handling difficult weather or road conditions confidently.
texts.33:
## Common Questions About Buying Used SUVs
### What maintenance costs should I expect with an SUV?
Mainstream SUVs cost $792-900 annually to maintain according to AAA data, comparable to sedan maintenance. This includes regular oil changes every 5,000-7,500 miles ($40-70 each), tire rotations, brake service, and routine inspections. Toyota and Honda lead with lowest costs: the RAV4 averages just $386 annually while the CR-V shows below-average repair frequency. The Mazda CX-5 requires only 0.6 unscheduled repair visits yearly. AWD systems add $200-500 annually compared to FWD vehicles due to additional components requiring service. Larger SUVs face higher tire replacement costs, with sets running $800-$1,500 compared to $600-$1,000 for compact SUVs. European luxury SUVs carry significantly higher costs: Mercedes-Benz maintenance runs double Lincoln's costs over 10 years, while Porsche averages $1,623 annually. Proper maintenance dramatically affects longevity. Follow the manufacturer's service schedule precisely, address minor issues promptly before they become expensive problems, and use quality parts. Well-maintained Toyotas and Hondas routinely exceed 200,000 miles with reasonable repair costs. Keep service records organized and address any unusual noises, vibrations, or warning lights immediately.
texts.34:
## Common Questions About Buying Used SUVs
### Do I need special features for upstate South Carolina weather?
Upstate South Carolina's humid subtropical climate requires specific considerations but not extreme weather equipment. The region receives 47-50 inches of annual rainfall, making AWD beneficial for confident driving in heavy rain and on wet roads, though quality FWD with good all-season tires proves adequate for most situations. AWD shows its value during occasional winter ice events and when accessing unpaved roads to outdoor recreation areas. Ground clearance of 8+ inches handles unpaved access roads to state park trailheads and boat launches without difficulty. Standard modern features address the climate well: working air conditioning proves essential during humid summers (test it thoroughly during purchase), rear climate vents keep passengers comfortable, and heated seats extend comfortable outdoor season into cooler months. The region's mild winters (rarely significant snow at 800-1,000 foot elevations) don't require the winter packages or extreme cold weather features needed in northern climates. Instead, prioritize features for the active outdoor lifestyle: roof rails for kayaks and bikes to area lakes and trails, easy-clean interior materials that tolerate dirt and water from outdoor activities, and adequate cargo space for camping gear. Quality all-season tires matter more than AWD for most drivers, though many buyers choose AWD for the 5-7% fuel economy penalty given the region's outdoor recreation emphasis.

## Common Questions About Buying Used SUVs
### Should I buy a hybrid SUV or stick with traditional gas engines?
Hybrid SUVs dramatically narrow the fuel economy gap with sedans while maintaining full SUV capability. The Toyota RAV4 Hybrid achieves 40 MPG combined versus 30 MPG for the gas model, saving approximately $600-800 annually for a driver covering 15,000 miles at $3.50/gallon. The Honda CR-V Hybrid reaches 38 MPG combined. These hybrids cost $3,000-5,000 more used than gas equivalents, but fuel savings recover this premium in 4-6 years while providing the same cargo space, seating, and towing capability. Hybrid systems prove particularly efficient in stop-and-go traffic and city driving, ideal for Spartanburg and Greenville commuters. Reliability concerns have largely disappeared with modern hybrids: Toyota's hybrid system has proven durable over 20+ years and millions of vehicles. Battery warranties typically cover 8-10 years or 100,000 miles. Maintenance costs run slightly higher due to additional components, but this difference is minor compared to fuel savings. The practical consideration is purchase price: if your budget allows the $3,000-5,000 hybrid premium on a used SUV, the fuel savings and reduced environmental impact make it worthwhile. If budget is tighter, a well-maintained gas SUV provides excellent service with slightly higher fuel costs but lower initial investment.

### **Introduction - Find the best Jeep deals!**
Jeepis a globally aspirational brand, defined mainly by the iconicWranglerand its ancestors. Top and doors off, the Wrangler epitomizes the rugged individualism and spirit of adventure that characterizes America and its citizens. It is a rolling symbol of fun, freedom, and determination. Unlike the Wrangler, the Grand Cherokee is a civilized daily driver, comfortable, quiet, and far more refined. You can't remove the roof and doors, but you'll also be a much happier camper most of the time.
Redesigned for 2022, the Grand Cherokee comes in two flavors. The first is the 2-row, 5-passenger version that is the subject of this review. The second is the 3-row, 7-passenger version that debuted in 2021. You canlearn more about the 2021 Jeep Grand Cherokee L by reading this full review of the SUV.
The 5-passenger 2022 Grand Cherokee lineup launches with Laredo, Altitude, Limited, Trailhawk, Overland, Summit, and Summit Reserve trim levels. texts.3:
### _Getting In and Getting Comfortable_
****
_**Photo: Christian Wardlaw**_
Unless you've raised the available Quadra-Lift airsuspensionto maximize ground clearance, as I did during an off-roading adventure in the Grand Cherokee Trailhawk, this SUV is easy enough to get into and out of. That's especially true if you kneel the SUV's air suspension using the Exit Mode, which drops the Grand Cherokee to its lowest setting in just seven seconds.
Regardless of the trim level, each test vehicle had a power-adjustable driver's seat that offered plenty of comfort and support. Even the cloth-upholstered Laredo had heated front seats and a heated steering wheel, and the Summit Reserve's supple premium leather chairs came with ventilation and a massage function.
Once you're aboard, you'll discover improved outward visibility compared to the previous-generation Grand Cherokee. Partly, this is due to the lower beltline and greater glass area. Still, the new Grand Cherokee also offers a variety of camera views, including a rear camera mirror and an off-roading camera that looks forward and, on the display screen, overlays the projected tire path onto the upcoming terrain.
The control layout is straightforward, but the gloss black trim in some models can suffer from reflections that make them hard to see and use. Also, Jeep uses a rotary knob for a shifter, and it took me a few tries to get the hang of it. Too often, I chose Drive instead of Park, released the brake, and started to get out before realizing the dang thing was moving.
A 10.25-inch digital instrumentation display is standard, and most versions include an 8.4-inch touchscreen infotainment system. A larger 10.1-inch screen is available in all but Laredo trim. Beneath the infotainment system, a mix of stereo and climate controls offers quick access to frequently used functions.
texts.4:
### _Getting In and Getting Comfortable_
Every version of the Grand Cherokee reflects quality. In fact, when you drive the Laredo, it feels more substantial than you expect of a base-trim model. Many vehicles feel engineered to a minimum standard and then get extra sound-deadening material, leather, wood, and technology in order to pass the premium test. By contrast, the new Grand Cherokee sounds and feels like it is built to a higher standard, and then Jeep figured out how to discount it to hit the Laredo's price point. In any case, if your budget dictates getting the Laredo, you won't feel like you settled for less.
Rear-seat room is tight for adults, and the hard plastic front seatbacks are painful when knees and shins encounter them. Grand Cherokee buyers who plan to transport taller passengers regularly will want the roomier Grand Cherokee L model.

Pairing my iPhone XS to Bluetooth was not a problem, and setting up personal preferences is relatively easy—especially if you're comfortable with modern technology. The voice-recognition system also works well, responding quickly and accurately to nearly all my standard test commands and questions.
There is a clear progression in terms of audio system quality. The basic setup in the Laredo was merely adequate, and the Alpine speakers in the Limited were an improvement. But they didn't come anywhere close to the outstanding McIntosh components in the Overland and Summit Reserve test vehicles.

Domestic brands like Ford and Chevrolet offer good value with reasonable reliability, though maintenance costs run slightly higher than Japanese brands. Avoid European luxury SUVs from Mercedes-Benz and BMW in the used market due to significantly higher repair costs.

## Common Questions About Buying Used SUVs
### What should I inspect when test driving a used SUV?
Begin by checking all features before driving: test air conditioning, heating, radio, power windows, locks, and windshield wipers. Verify the backup camera displays clearly and that all interior lights function. Check that the liftgate opens and closes smoothly. Start the engine and listen for smooth, quiet operation without knocking, ticking, or unusual noises. During the test drive, accelerate firmly to ensure the engine responds without hesitation and the transmission shifts smoothly through all gears. Drive on highways to check for vibrations at 60-70 MPH and verify the cruise control works properly. Test brakes multiple times, ensuring the pedal feels firm and the SUV stops straight without pulling to either side. Make several turns to check steering responsiveness. If the SUV has AWD, verify the system engages properly (some vehicles have indicators or test modes). Check for adequate power when accelerating from a stop, especially important in three-row SUVs carrying passengers. Pay attention to visibility from the driver's seat, blind spots, and whether mirrors provide clear views. Listen for wind noise at highway speeds and rattles over bumps. After the test drive, check under the SUV for any fluid leaks.

## Common Questions About Buying Used SUVs
### Are SUVs really safer than sedans?
SUVs provide several safety advantages that combine structural benefits with modern technology. The elevated seating position improves visibility, allowing drivers to see traffic patterns, hazards, and brake lights farther ahead than sedan drivers sitting 6-12 inches lower. Greater size and weight reduce collision forces on occupants during impacts. Modern SUVs include comprehensive safety technology as standard equipment: automatic emergency braking with pedestrian detection, blind-spot monitoring with rear cross-traffic alert, and lane keeping assist have become baseline features on most 2018-2020 models. Statistics support this perception, with 58% of SUV buyers reporting feeling safer in larger vehicles. Insurance costs reflect actual safety performance, with SUVs averaging $1,935 annually versus $2,120 for sedans, a $185 annual savings indicating lower injury claim rates. However, proper safety depends on vehicle condition and driver behavior more than vehicle type. Any well-maintained SUV or sedan with modern safety features provides excellent protection. The IIHS and NHTSA test both vehicle types rigorously, and top-rated sedans and SUVs perform comparably in crashes. The practical advantage of SUVs comes from better visibility and handling difficult weather or road conditions confidently.

## Common Questions About Buying Used SUVs
### What maintenance costs should I expect with an SUV?
Mainstream SUVs cost $792-900 annually to maintain according to AAA data, comparable to sedan maintenance. This includes regular oil changes every 5,000-7,500 miles ($40-70 each), tire rotations, brake service, and routine inspections. Toyota and Honda lead with lowest costs: the RAV4 averages just $386 annually while the CR-V shows below-average repair frequency. The Mazda CX-5 requires only 0.6 unscheduled repair visits yearly. AWD systems add $200-500 annually compared to FWD vehicles due to additional components requiring service. Larger SUVs face higher tire replacement costs, with sets running $800-$1,500 compared to $600-$1,000 for compact SUVs. European luxury SUVs carry significantly higher costs: Mercedes-Benz maintenance runs double Lincoln's costs over 10 years, while Porsche averages $1,623 annually. Proper maintenance dramatically affects longevity. Follow the manufacturer's service schedule precisely, address minor issues promptly before they become expensive problems, and use quality parts. Well-maintained Toyotas and Hondas routinely exceed 200,000 miles with reasonable repair costs. Keep service records organized and address any unusual noises, vibrations, or warning lights immediately.

## Common Questions About Buying Used SUVs
### Do I need special features for upstate South Carolina weather?
Upstate South Carolina's humid subtropical climate requires specific considerations but not extreme weather equipment. The region receives 47-50 inches of annual rainfall, making AWD beneficial for confident driving in heavy rain and on wet roads, though quality FWD with good all-season tires proves adequate for most situations. AWD shows its value during occasional winter ice events and when accessing unpaved roads to outdoor recreation areas. Ground clearance of 8+ inches handles unpaved access roads to state park trailheads and boat launches without difficulty. Standard modern features address the climate well: working air conditioning proves essential during humid summers (test it thoroughly during purchase), rear climate vents keep passengers comfortable, and heated seats extend comfortable outdoor season into cooler months. The region's mild winters (rarely significant snow at 800-1,000 foot elevations) don't require the winter packages or extreme cold weather features needed in northern climates. Instead, prioritize features for the active outdoor lifestyle: roof rails for kayaks and bikes to area lakes and trails, easy-clean interior materials that tolerate dirt and water from outdoor activities, and adequate cargo space for camping gear. Quality all-season tires matter more than AWD for most drivers, though many buyers choose AWD for the 5-7% fuel economy penalty given the region's outdoor recreation emphasis.

## Common Questions About Buying Used SUVs
### Should I buy a hybrid SUV or stick with traditional gas engines?
Hybrid SUVs dramatically narrow the fuel economy gap with sedans while maintaining full SUV capability. The Toyota RAV4 Hybrid achieves 40 MPG combined versus 30 MPG for the gas model, saving approximately $600-800 annually for a driver covering 15,000 miles at $3.50/gallon. The Honda CR-V Hybrid reaches 38 MPG combined. These hybrids cost $3,000-5,000 more used than gas equivalents, but fuel savings recover this premium in 4-6 years while providing the same cargo space, seating, and towing capability. Hybrid systems prove particularly efficient in stop-and-go traffic and city driving, ideal for Spartanburg and Greenville commuters. Reliability concerns have largely disappeared with modern hybrids: Toyota's hybrid system has proven durable over 20+ years and millions of vehicles. Battery warranties typically cover 8-10 years or 100,000 miles. Maintenance costs run slightly higher due to additional components, but this difference is minor compared to fuel savings. The practical consideration is purchase price: if your budget allows the $3,000-5,000 hybrid premium on a used SUV, the fuel savings and reduced environmental impact make it worthwhile. If budget is tighter, a well-maintained gas SUV provides excellent service with slightly higher fuel costs but lower initial investment.
